Have you ever been invited for a drink at a French friend’s home, heard someone say they have un petit creux, and wondered how you would even translate that? It happens to almost everyone, and it doesn’t mean your French is bad. Some of the coziest words of daily life in France simply don’t have a neat English match, because they come from the way French people eat and gather around the table.

In this video I’ll go through the little food words I use every day, like le goûter, l’apéro, grignoter and se régaler, and the small cultural rules hiding behind them. Then we’ll practice a few easy sentences out loud together, so you know exactly what to say the next time you’re a guest at a French table.
